slides.headline: He built drug-delivery technology now in clinical trials. In 2026, America's medical academy took notice.
Ashutosh Chilkoti was elected to the US National Academy of Medicine's 2026 class
slides.body: The Duke University biomedical engineering professor was recognized for developing the first artificial polypeptides to enter clinical trials for sustained protein-drug delivery, announced October 19, 2026.

slides.headline: Born in India, he earned his B.Tech in Chemical Engineering from IIT Delhi in 1985 before joining Duke's faculty in 1996.
slides.body: Now the Alan L. Kaganov Distinguished Professor of Biomedical Engineering, his work spans protein purification and PEGylation technology used in treatments worldwide.

slides.eyebrow: Why it matters for Viksit Bharat 2047
slides.headline: A Viksit Bharat benefits when an India-trained engineer's lab work becomes medicine already reaching patients.
slides.body: Chilkoti's election is a reminder that India's engineering pipeline feeds directly into the institutions that set the terms of global medicine.
